title: U-lock a bike wheel to a stand with an angled bent-foot engagement
instruction: Lock the bike's back wheel to the bike stand with the U-lock.
context: Locking a bicycle wheel to a fixed street stand requires linking both objects and closing the lock. Here two arms handle a full-size bent-foot U-lock around a child's 12-inch rear wheel and a Sheffield stand. One end must pass between spokes, the other outside the tyre. The crossbar must first receive the outwardly bent foot through its narrow mouth, then pivot onto the straight end; aligned simultaneous insertion hits the retaining lip. This is a representative bent-foot mechanism, distinct from a hinged padlock snapped through one hole. The goal secures the wheel; it does not claim theft protection for the entire bicycle.
setup: The table top stands for the pavement. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Bike: a child's bike with 12-inch wheels (ISO 203 rims, 57-203 tyres, 31.7 cm across; 16 radial 2 mm steel spokes per wheel, aluminium rim 17-20 cm across), red steel frame, standing on its kickstand; its frame and front wheel are fixed in place. Its wheelbase is 48 cm, shorter than the 58 to 60 cm of real 12-inch bikes, so that the whole bike fits on the table; the wheels and tyres are true size. It faces away from the robot to the left: its back hub is at x 38, y -1, 15.9 cm up, its front hub at x 58.3, y 42.5. The back wheel turns freely on its axle (0.8 kg, light bearing drag); at the start two spokes sit 11.25 degrees above and below the horizontal line from the hub toward the back of the bike. Stand: a fixed, full-size Sheffield cycle stand of 48 mm galvanised steel tube, 75 cm tall, standing on the table top, legs 70 cm apart (commercial stands are about 75 to 100 cm long), standing parallel to the bike between it and the robot; one leg is at x 26.5, y -11.3, 8 mm in front of the back tyre and 14.2 cm from the hub along the bike, the other at x 56.1, y 52.1. U-lock (the size and mass of a common standard 4 x 9 inch U-lock such as a Kryptonite KryptoLok Standard: nominal bare-rod clearance 10.2 cm, sleeve clearance 9.47 cm, closed internal depth about 22 cm, 12.7 mm hardened steel shackle, 1.32 kg in all), lying flat in two parts. Shackle: 0.62 kg, a vinyl sleeve 20 mm across over the bend and the first 7 cm of each leg, the rest bare steel; it lies with its bend toward the robot at x 13, y 17 (centre of the bend), legs pointing away from the robot parallel to the bike. Crossbar: 0.70 kg nominal lumped mass, steel core with black rigid polymer casing 40 x 40 mm, 18 cm long, plus a 5 cm cylindrical lock head at its outer end. Socket axes 11.47 cm apart, mouths 20 x 20 mm toward the robot. At x 25, y -30 cm, lying flat with the same yaw as the shackle. The outer shackle leg bends outward: from x=183 mm at its leg axis to a toe centre at x=198 mm, 16 mm outward; 12.7 mm rod throughout. The outer socket has an 8 mm thick retaining lip, a 20 mm mouth and an enlarged inner chamber. The inner straight socket has a 25 mm deep bottom. The bar first enters at an angle around the bent foot, then pivots onto the straight end. It fits one orientation. Key operation is omitted: a fixed joint engages only when the straight end is 21 to 25.5 mm inside the mouth and within 3 mm laterally, and the toe is within 3 mm of its final chamber centre, with bounded axial seating. All dimensions are representative, not a commercial product replica. Fixed layout; no randomisation.
scoring: Read at the end, from a photo and by hand. The lock goes round the rim if the rim passes through the closed lock (the shackle including its bent foot and the crossbar closing its ends): the wheel cannot be removed without opening the lock. It goes round the stand if the stand's leg or top bar passes through it. Locked: the crossbar is on both leg ends and has caught (straight end 21 to 25.5 mm inside its mouth and within 3 mm laterally, bent toe within 3 mm of its final chamber centre and bounded axially); once caught it stays on, as a real crossbar does without its key. 1.0: locked, round both the rim and the stand, every finger of both grippers at least 3 cm from both lock parts and both parts moving less than 2 mm over the last second, held for 1 s. 0.5: the same lock, correctly closed round both the rim and the stand, but a gripper is still on it or it is still moving. 0.25: not locked, but the shackle passes round both the rim and the stand (threaded correctly, crossbar missing or not pushed home). Otherwise 0, including a lock closed round only the rim or only the stand, and a shackle with both legs between the spokes, inside the rim.
reset_notes: Disable the latch, restore both parts to their marked flat starting poses and turn the rear wheel to its initial spoke angle. Simulation reset clears latch and score history.
fidelity: Rigid primitive geometry with real collisions: 12.7 mm bent-foot shackle, narrow socket mouth, retaining lip and enlarged chamber require angled crossbar engagement. Representative dimensions, not a product replica. Key/bolt motion is replaced by a fixed joint at bounded final seating; no angle/history gate. Bike wheelbase shortened to 48 cm; frame fixed, rear wheel rotates. Tyre rigid; pad friction 1.0; no force cap.
scores: Dream-1 beta seed 1: 0.0 (1,200 actions); scripted demo: 1.0 (940 actions). Both use this revised scene and scorer; post-demo reset passed.
